confidence_notes: I ran six web searches: one for the RBA rate and five for Denver food and drink prices. Inexpensive meal, mid-range meal for two, beer and coffee rest on aggregated, crowdsourced figures: Numbeo data republished by Expatica for June 2026, an American Craft Beer median of $7.02 for March 2026, and Expatistan and cafe menu prices. I rounded these to restaurant-level prices, since tax and tip push bar prices higher. Cocktail and wine are less certain. I found only an Expatistan guess of about $16 for a downtown club cocktail and happy-hour deals of about $8. I found no per-glass wine average, so wine is set at roughly 1.8x the restaurant beer price. Accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for a July 2026 summer-season window. They come from general knowledge, with no accommodation searches and no live listings checked. Denver has few registered hostels, so the hostel figures are especially uncertain. The FX observation comes from a search summary of RBA pages. I did not open the page myself, and some cached RBA pages showed older dates and rates, so I used the 18 November 2026 observation that the search reported.
comparable_city_reasoning: Denver prices are close to other mid-to-high-cost U.S. Mountain West and West Coast mid-sized cities such as Portland, Seattle (slightly lower) and Salt Lake City (slightly higher). They sit at the upper end of the national mid-sized range. Food and drink anchors are anchored on Denver-specific aggregates. Accommodation reflects Denver's summer tourism demand.
